# Review verdict — Sprint 3, work unit 18, registered PR 15

**Verdict: approved**
**PR:** https://github.com/jedbjorn/subfloor/pull/1063
**Reviewed head:** e6361f7db2d842b32b5dc8ef8b9a53d0f6e5ceb2 (exact bound head)
**Spec:** #116 @ 400fc63cbf2f9d3d3c885fd9f35d07d3d7ddce03926c5ea8b2fae5085df66aa4 (QAQC approval 9, pass)
**Scope:** task #352 — source-only installed-fork Sprint canary

## Findings

No Critical, Major, or Medium findings.

**Low (report note, non-blocking):** the failure receipt's run-state evidence is
bounded to the board's pickup/delivery projections plus pause reason on the
`CANARY_SPRINT_FAILED` path; per-conversation run states are not captured
verbatim on every failure boundary. The receipt still carries stable CanaryError
codes, stage, pickup action, and bounded board evidence, which is sufficient for
diagnosis. Deepening per-conversation run-state capture is a resilience
improvement, not a correctness gap in the delivered behavior.

## Code quality

Traced the real paths, not the names:

- `maintainer/` is confirmed outside `ENGINE_PATHS`
  (`.super-coder/scripts/engine_manifest.py:56`); no `sc` verb was added, and
  `test_maintainer_command_is_not_distributed_or_added_as_sc_verb` guards both
  via AST literal-eval of the manifest plus a dispatcher scan.
- Container naming matches the live dispatcher: `CNAME="sc-$(basename $here)"`
  (`dispatch.sh:126`) equals the ledger's `sc-<workspace.name>`; `SC_NET`
  overrides the network (`dispatch.sh:130`), so launch, preflight collision
  checks, and cleanup all name the same real resources. Ports land in the
  8800–8899 band consistent with `ports.py` and are held bound from preflight
  until launch, closing the obvious race.
- `sc harness-status` docker-execs `harness_versions.py` inside the sandbox
  (`dispatch.sh:247`), so recorded harness versions are launched-runtime
  provenance, not host binaries — exactly what spec item 2 demands.
- Cleanup identity guards are real: branch deletes require the
  `subfloor-canary/<run_id>/` prefix, container/network names must equal the
  expected derived names, workspace removal requires the marker file binding
  run_id and candidate SHA, and a foreign PR identity refuses close
  (`test_cleanup_refuses_a_pr_whose_remote_identity_does_not_match` turns this
  red). Cleanup failure is fatal and preserves the primary failure
  (`test_cleanup_failure_is_fatal_and_preserves_primary_failure`).
- The receipt write is atomic (mkstemp + fsync + replace) and recursively
  redacted; hermetic tests prove secret values never reach disk.

## Edge cases and gaps

- Deadline model verified: per-stage deadlines reset on genuine board-signature
  progress but remain capped by the whole-run deadline; cleanup gets its own
  bounded grace so a whole-run timeout cannot strand resources. Covered by
  `test_deadlines_enforce_stage_whole_run_and_cleanup_grace`.
- Preflight-before-writes is proven: no receipt, workspace, branch, or container
  exists when preflight refuses
  (`test_preflight_failure_happens_before_every_resource_write`).
- Checked the one sequencing risk against live state: the preflight gate refuses
  a live dos-app with any prepared/armed/paused Sprint, while task #353 runs the
  canary before dos-app Sprint 5 recovery. Verified the live dos-app engine DB
  directly — Sprint 5 is now `aborted`, so the gate does not conflict with the
  current floor. No finding.
- Postgres sidecar cannot leak: it only starts with a `pg` key in instance.json
  (`dispatch.sh:928`); the disposable install's fresh instance.json has none.

## Spec conformance (spec #116, "Installed-fork canary" section)

- Disposable copy at exact base with isolated DB/namespace/ports/worktrees; live
  dos-app DB never used for the Sprint — conforms (items 1–2).
- Candidate resolved to one commit, materialized via exact-SHA refspec, engine
  pin and callable `sc engine-ref` both asserted — conforms; hermetic test
  proves the refspec and pin check.
- Codex Planner with nullable model/effort (exercises #1056), Kimi Reviewer
  (exercises #1055), closed originating Planner chat forcing a fresh Re-enter
  whose route must be canonical non-null — conforms (items 3–4).
- Ephemeral base/head branches only, main-isolation proven by merge-base against
  origin/main; real PR, real pickup chain to `lifecycle.completed` with no
  synthetic rows possible (public API + prompts only) — conforms (items 5–6).
- Stage/whole deadlines fail closed; sanitized durable receipt preserved outside
  disposable state under gitignored `shared/`; idempotent cleanup with a rerun
  subcommand — conforms (items 7–8).
- Lane boundary honored: no live receipt, no dos-app install update, no Sprint 5
  recovery claimed — those remain task #353.

## Verification evidence

- All six CI checks pass at the exact reviewed head (tests, verify,
  render-check, CodeQL ×2 + suite).
- Locally at the reviewed head: `python3 -m unittest
  tests.test_dos_app_sprint_canary` — 12/12 OK; `tests.test_sprint_removal_manifest` —
  14/14 OK (fixture manifest consistently extended for the new test file).
- PR body contains only the work-unit id and spec reference; readiness body was
  a bare locator. Protocol clean.

items.expected_output:
A reviewed and merged source-only subfloor maintainer canary outside
`ENGINE_PATHS`, with no distributed `sc` verb. The implementation must include
hermetic coverage for preflight, exact-ref materialization, orchestration,
deadlines, receipt redaction, partial-failure cleanup, and idempotent cleanup.
The post-merge live receipt and dos-app Sprint 5 recovery remain task #353 and
are not claimed by this editing lane.
